_about: Field terms for F114, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

ring-channel.field: dendrochronology, our usage after the channel of information theory
ring-channel.definition: one quantity measured in every annual ring of a site's trees and kept as a yearly series: ring width, earlywood width, latewood width, minimum density or maximum latewood density
ring-channel.excludes: a climate variable, and a combination of several measured quantities

mxd.definition: the highest wood density in the late, dense part of an annual ring, read from an X-ray image of a thin lath of the core
mxd.excludes: ring width and the mean density of the whole ring

bit.definition: the unit of information: one bit halves the uncertainty about an outcome, so a record that keeps b bits a year narrows each year's range of possible summers by a factor of 2 to the power b, as measured by its standard deviation
bit.excludes: a count of stored numbers, and any statement about which way the dependence runs

ce.field: hydrology and dendroclimatology; also called the Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency
ce.definition: one minus the mean squared error of a reconstruction on held-out years divided by the variance of the true values in those years; 1 is perfect and 0 means no better than the held-out years' own mean
ce.excludes: a correlation, which ignores bias and scale errors

re.definition: the same as the coefficient of efficiency, except that the reference is the mean of the calibration years, so it rewards getting a shift in mean right
re.excludes: a score computed on the years used to fit the model

block-cv.definition: the years are split into contiguous blocks, here five; each block in turn is held out, the model is fitted on the rest and scored on the held-out block
block-cv.excludes: a score on the fitting years, and splits that scatter single years so that neighbouring years leak into the fit

mutual-information.definition: the reduction in uncertainty about one variable from knowing another, in bits, which counts any dependence and not only linear dependence
mutual-information.excludes: a measure of the size of a slope or of causation

ksg.definition: the k-nearest-neighbour estimate of mutual information from samples given by Kraskov, Stoegbauer and Grassberger, here with 4 neighbours
ksg.excludes: estimates that first bin the data into histograms

eps.definition: how well the mean of k series stands for the mean of an infinite set of such series, k r over 1 plus (k minus 1) r, with r the mean correlation between series; 0.85 is the conventional threshold
eps.excludes: a measure of how well the series track climate

high-pass.definition: a filter that keeps fast variation and removes slow trends; here each series minus a Gaussian smooth of width 10 years, which keeps roughly the 2 to 30 year band

phase-randomisation.definition: a copy of a series with the same power spectrum and random Fourier phases, so it keeps the series' autocorrelation and loses its timing against any other series
phase-randomisation.excludes: shuffling years, which also destroys the autocorrelation

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

site-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by recomputing a network mean many times on sites drawn with replacement from the panel, so the spread reflects differences between sites
site-bootstrap.excludes: an interval over years or over model refits at one site
